Caption / description / post text:
My updated honeybaked ham recipe! This has become such a hit with not only my all my friends and family but also yours, & I’m so honored! This recipe is insanely low effort & the pinnacle of heavenly! Enjoy!🤎 Full recipe is on elizabethsrecipediary.com🤎 Please lmk if you have questions!🤗 Ingredients: -1 spiral sliced ham -1 cup pineapple juice -4 tbsps melted butter -4 tbsps @Mike’s Hot Honey -1.5 cup granulated sugar -3 cups dark brown sugar -1.5 tsps tsp @Lawry’s Seasoning salt -1.5 tsps garlic powder -1 tbsp cinnamon -1.5 tsps nutmeg -1.5 tsps cloves -1.5 tsps ground ginger -1.5 tsps paprika -1 tsp all spice -2 tbsps Dijon mustard -1 tbsp apple cider vinegar -1 tbsp soy sauce 1. Place your ham flat side down on a roasting rack. Brush it with a mix of melted butter & the hot honey. Pour 1 cup of pineapple juice into the bottom of the pan.  2. Cover the ham with foil, & bake it at 275 F for 8 minutes per pound of ham (mine was 11 lbs, so I baked it for about 1 hour & 30 minutes). 3. Once the ham is finished baking, reserve 3 tbsps of the ham drippings. 4. Combine the sugars, seasoned salt, garlic powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, ground ginger, sweet paprika, and all spice. Split the sugar mixture equally into 3 bowls. 5. Pat 1 bowl (⅓ of the total sugar mix) of the sugar mixture over the ham. Make sure to get it into the crevices as well 6. Broil the ham on high uncovered for 2 minutes. 7. Remove the ham from the oven, & pat the second bowl of sugar mixture evenly over the ham. 8. Broil the ham on high again for 2 minutes. 9. Remove ham from the oven, & reserve 1 cup of the ham drippings. 10. For the glaze, in a sauce pan, combine the ham drippings, remaining sugar mixture (the final third of the mixture), soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, and Dijon mustard. Bring it to a boil, and remove it from the heat. 11. Brush the glaze over the ham, and broil it again for 2-3 minutes until bubbly and crispy.  #honeybakedham #thanksgiving #thanksgivingdinner #tiktokthanksgivingcontest #recipe @Kerrygold USA @Caraway Home @HexClad @McCormick Spices @McCormick Gourmet @Foodlion @Costco Wholesale @Cuisinart @target @Kikkoman USA @Wegmans 

Transcript of the video's audio (machine-made):
Every year, it physically pains me to watch people pay over $200 for a honey baked ham when it's insanely easy to make at home. This recipe is so much better, juicier, and more flavorful than the store-bought version, so save your money and let me show you how to make it yourself. This is my viral honey baked ham recipe that has over 13 million views across all platforms, and many of you have told me that it's now a holiday staple in your family, and I am so honored. You want to buy a smoked, spiralized ham? I buy mine from Costco for just $26. It's already pre-cooked and pre-sliced, so it makes your life so much easier. First, take that brown sugar packet that comes with it and throw it away. Lay your ham flat side down on a roasting rack and pour in one cup of pineapple juice because duh, ham and pineapple match made in heaven. The flavors are going to infuse into your ham and serve as the most magical glaze later on. Mix 4 tablespoons of melted butter and hot honey together and brush it all over your ham and in between the crevices. Cover your ham with foil and warm it up in the oven at 275 for 8 minutes per every pound. My ham was 11 pounds, so I baked it for an hour and 30 minutes. Now, this is how we're going to get that signature brown sugar crust that's going to get all crispy and caramelized in the oven. Mix together white sugar, dark brown sugar, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and I don't feel like listing the rest, but you can read. And if you think this is a lot of sugar, look, it's the holiday season. If you want to eat healthy, you're going to be eating alone. Split your sugar mixture into three equal portions and smother a third of it all over your warmed up ham and nicely into the crevices. We're going to violate it real well. All right, we're going to do three rounds of two minute broils to achieve that crispy caramelized crust. Broil your ham for two minutes and then cover it again with another third of the sugar mixture. Then broil again for another two minutes until the sugar crust is bubbly and crispy. Before your final broil, reserve one cup of the ham drippings and because we threw away that brown sugar glaze packet, we're going to make one that's 10 times better. Mix in your ham drippings, Dijon, apple cider vinegar, and of course soy sauce because this is an Asian household. No, really, though, you can't taste it, but it's going to add an earthy balance of flavor. Pour in your remaining sugar mixture, bring to a boil, and then remove it from the heat. Bave that magical glaze all over your ham and broil for one last time for two minutes. And by this point, your ham should be glistening like it just descended from heaven. Guys, this golden brown sugar crust is a delicacy in itself. The ham is juicy, melt in your mouth tender, and the pineapple juice adds the perfect balance of flavors to the fatty savory ham. As someone who ate honey baked ham all the time growing up, I can confidently say that this is so much better and it will make you wonder why people spend so much money on a mediocre version of this.
